Thus it subsumes single-denomination budgets, but the covering principle is the cost function abstraction.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The linear form may not capture non-linear resource constraints (e.g., fixed request overhead plus per-byte cost), but a more general cost function could be used.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The agent is configured with a cost function C(req, bytes) = \u03b1*req + \u03b2*bytes, with \u03b1,\u03b2 \u2265 0. It maintains a total_cost counter. Before each fetch, it estimates the cost of the planned fetch and checks if total_cost + estimated_cost > max_cost. If so, it records a terminal event with type 'budget_exhausted', the cost function, max_cost, total_cost, and the sequence of (req, bytes) per fetch for audit. The state hash includes the cost function parameters but not the running total.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
